```{r define-functions, include = FALSE}
# Define functions

## Reads in Data from all sheets at once + manipulation to extract only relevant data
read_all <- function(filename, tibble = TRUE) {
    # If tibble is preferred over data.frame use "tibble = TRUE"
    sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(filename)
    x <- lapply(sheets, function(y) readxl::read_excel(filename, sheet = y))
    x <- lapply(x, function(y) as.data.frame(y))
    x <- lapply(x, function(y) y %>% mutate(., across(where(is.character), as.factor)))
    names(x) <- sheets
    x
}

## Define function to run survival analysis, pairwise comparison and produce asterisks
fit_peto <- function(x, group_var) {
  # Define the formula
  f <- as.formula(sprintf("Surv(Hours_pi, Event) ~ %s", group_var))
  # Pairwise comparison
  pw <- survminer::pairwise_survdiff(
    f, # Input the formula
    data = x, # Input the data
    p.adjust.method = "BH", # Adjust p-values for multiple comparision with FDR correction
    rho = 1 # NOTE: rho = 1 calls the Peto-Peto modification of the Gehan-Wilcoxon test
  )
  # Put data together for output
  list(
    "Survival" = survival::survdiff(f, data = x, rho = 1),
    "Pairwise" = pw,
    "Asterisks" = symnum(
      pw$p.value,
      cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
      symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "+", " "),
      abbr.colnames = FALSE,
      na = ""
    )
  )
}

## function for the Cox proportional hazards model containing tt() as dummy variabls
fit_cox_tt <- function(xx) {
  
  mm <- model.matrix(~ Infestation, data = xx)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  colnames(mm) <- make.names(colnames(mm))
  
  x2 <- dplyr::bind_cols(xx, as.data.frame(mm))
  
  dummy_names <- colnames(mm)
  level_map <- tibble::tibble(
    Infestation = levels(xx$Infestation)[-1],
    dummy = dummy_names
  )
  
  main_terms <- paste(dummy_names, collapse = " + ")
  tt_terms   <- paste0("tt(", dummy_names, ")", collapse = " + ")
  
  form <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      "Surv(Hours_pi, Event) ~ ",
      main_terms,
      " + ",
      tt_terms,
      " + frailty(Guinea_Pig, distribution = 'gaussian', sparse = TRUE, method = 'reml')"
    )
  )
  
  tt_fun <- function(z, t, ...) {
    z * log(pmax(t, 1))
  }
  
  fit <- survival::coxph(
    form,
    data = x2,
    x = TRUE,
    y = TRUE,
    model = FALSE,
    ties = "efron",
    tt = rep(list(tt_fun), length(dummy_names))
  )
  
  attr(fit, "Infestation_levels") <- levels(xx$Infestation)
  attr(fit, "level_map") <- level_map
  attr(fit, "dummy_names") <- dummy_names
  
  fit
}

## Pairwise comparison for models containg tt()
pairwise_tt_contrasts <- function(fit, times = c(24, 48, 72),
                                  adjust = "BH",
                                  adjust_within_time = TRUE) {
  
  levs <- attr(fit, "Infestation_levels")
  level_map <- attr(fit, "level_map")
  dummy_names <- attr(fit, "dummy_names")
  
  beta <- stats::coef(fit)
  V <- stats::vcov(fit)
  
  needed_coef <- c(dummy_names, paste0("tt(", dummy_names, ")"))
  needed_coef <- intersect(needed_coef, names(beta))
  
  beta <- beta[needed_coef]
  V <- V[needed_coef, needed_coef, drop = FALSE]
  
  make_lp_vector <- function(level, time) {
    
    v <- rep(0, length(beta))
    names(v) <- names(beta)
    
    # Reference level has all zero coefficients
    if (level == levs[1]) {
      return(v)
    }
    
    d <- level_map$dummy[level_map$Infestation == level]
    
    main_name <- d
    tt_name <- paste0("tt(", d, ")")
    
    if (main_name %in% names(v)) {
      v[main_name] <- 1
    }
    
    if (tt_name %in% names(v)) {
      v[tt_name] <- log(pmax(time, 1))
    }
    
    v
  }
  
  out <- purrr::map_dfr(times, function(ttime) {
    
    pairs <- utils::combn(levs, 2, simplify = FALSE)
    
    purrr::map_dfr(pairs, function(pair) {
      
      level_1 <- pair[1]
      level_2 <- pair[2]
      
      v1 <- make_lp_vector(level_1, ttime)
      v2 <- make_lp_vector(level_2, ttime)
      contrast_vec <- v1 - v2
      
      log_hr <- sum(contrast_vec * beta)
      se <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(contrast_vec) %*% V %*% contrast_vec))
      z <- log_hr / se
      p <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(z))
      
      tibble::tibble(
        Hours_pi = ttime,
        contrast = paste(level_1, "vs", level_2),
        log_HR = log_hr,
        SE = se,
        z = z,
        p.value = p,
        HR = exp(log_hr),
        lower.CL = exp(log_hr - 1.96 * se),
        upper.CL = exp(log_hr + 1.96 * se)
      )
    })
  })
  
  if (adjust_within_time) {
    out <- out |>
      dplyr::group_by(Hours_pi) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        p.adj = stats::p.adjust(p.value, method = adjust)
      ) |>
      dplyr::ungroup()
  } else {
    out <- out |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        p.adj = stats::p.adjust(p.value, method = adjust)
      )
  }
  
  out %>%
    mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
    mutate(., across("p.value", ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", .x))) %>%
    mutate(., across("p.adj", ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", .x)))
  
  out 
}

## Fixed proportional hazard assumption test 
safe_cox_zph <- function(fit) {
  tryCatch(survival::cox.zph(fit), # H0: Tests for no significant deviation from slope = 0
           error = function(e) e)
}
## Fixed proportional hazard assumption test plot
safe_ggcoxzph <- function(zph) {
  if (inherits(zph, "error")) return("Error occurred")
  tryCatch(survminer::ggcoxzph(zph), error = function(e) "Error occurred")
}

## Compares different version of the Cox proportional hazard model
compare_cox_models <- function(models) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(models, function(fit, nm) {
    
    aic_val <- tryCatch(AIC(fit), error = function(e) NA_real_)
    edf_val <- tryCatch(extractAIC(fit)[1], error = function(e) NA_real_)
    
    y <- fit$y
    event_col <- ncol(y)
    
    tibble::tibble(
      model = nm,
      n_rows = nrow(y),
      events = sum(y[, event_col]),
      loglik = tail(fit$loglik, 1),
      edf = edf_val,
      AIC = aic_val,
      concordance = summary(fit)$concordance[1],
      concordance_se = summary(fit)$concordance[2]
    )
  })
}

# Makes decision on whether to a time interaction for the Cox PH model
DecisionMaking <- function(Table, AIC) {
  
  print(Table)
  print(AIC)
  
  # prompts selection of number corresponding to transformation
    aa <- readline("Choose how to continue:
                   1 = Mod_cluster
                   2 = Mod_frailty
                   3 = Mod_frailty_tt")
    
    # Insures permissive input is given
    if (as.numeric(aa) == 1) {
      
      aa <- 1
      
    } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 2) {
      
      aa <- 2
      
    } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 3) {
      
      aa <- 3
      } else {
      
      print("Wrong input")
      stop()
    }
    
    aa
}
```

```{r time-to-event-data-loading, include = FALSE}
# LOADING DATA #################################################################

## Get data directory
survival_dir <- file.path(here::here(), RawDat, RawDatSub)
## List all excel files in directory as full directory names
survival_files <- list.files(survival_dir, pattern = "\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE)

## Stop the script if no files are found
stopifnot(length(survival_files) >= 1)

## Load all data from all files contained within the directory
DatSur_list <- purrr::map(survival_files, read_all)
## Adjust the structure of data list
DatSur <- if (length(DatSur_list) == 1L) {
  DatSur_list[[1L]]
} else {
  purrr::imap(DatSur_list, function(x, file) {
    prefix <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file))
    stats::setNames(x, paste(prefix, names(x), sep = "__"))
  }) |>
    purrr::list_flatten()
} 

## Make adjustment to data table where new group means are required or two variables need to be merged as group names 
DatSur <- DatSur %>%
  lapply(., function(x) { # In cases where multiple variables need to be fused to a single group variable
    
    if (x %>% # In cases where multiple variables need to be fused to a single group variable
        dplyr::select(any_of(c("Infestation", "Treatment"))) %>% # Check if both columns are present
        ncol(.) >= 2) {
      
      x %>%
        mutate(., "Infestation_Round" = .$Infestation) %>% # Retain original Infestation variable
        mutate(., across(Infestation, ~paste0(x$Infestation, "_", x$Treatment))) %>% # Create new group names under "Infestation" by merging "Infestation" and "Treatment" variables
        mutate(., across(where(is.character), as.factor)) # Convert all character columns into factors
    } else {
      x
    }
  }) %>% 
  # Rearrange factor levels so we compare to the desired control group
  imap(~if (str_detect(.y, "E_collar")) {
    .x %>% mutate(Infestation = factor(Infestation, levels = c("Unrestricted", "Restricted")))
  } else {
    .x
  }) %>%
  imap(~if (str_detect(.y, "FTY720")) {
    .x %>% mutate(Infestation = factor(Infestation, levels = c("1st_PBS", "1st_FTY720", "2nd_PBS", "2nd_FTY720")))
  } else {
    .x
  })

## Adjust variables to factors, where needed
DatSur <- lapply(DatSur, function(xx) {
  xx %>%
    mutate(., across(any_of(c("Guinea_Pig", "Infestation", "Repeat", "Treatment")), as.factor))
})

# Tidy up what you do not need anymore
rm(survival_dir, survival_files, DatSur_list)
```

```{r cox-proportional-hazard-model, include = FALSE, cache = TRUE, cache.extra = file.mtime('Survival_Data.xlsx'), dev = 'png', fig.show = 'hide'}
# Cox proportional hazard model ---------------------------------------------
## This assess two things, whether guinea pigs represent a level two unit as multiple ticks are placed per guinea pig, and that guinea pigs were repeatedly used in consecutive infestations
ResCox <- DatSur %>%
  lapply(., function(x) {

  # This is the section on Cox PH model variation testing to identify the best model for the data
    #As the study design places multiple ticks per guinea pig, there may be potential clustering that needs to be considered. This can be address by including a clustering or frailty term in the equation. It is also possible that the proportional hazards assumption is not met. In this case we need to include a tt() term that allows for the proportional hazard to change over time.  
    
    ## Cluster-robust inference for repeated ticks within guinea pig
    CoxPH_cluster <- survival::coxph(Surv(Hours_pi, Event) ~ Infestation,
                                     data = x,
                                     x = TRUE,
                                     y = TRUE,
                                     ties = "efron",
                                     cluster = x$Guinea_Pig
                                     )
    
    ## Frailty model as random-effect sensitivity / heterogeneity check
    CoxPH_frailty <- survival::coxph(Surv(Hours_pi, Event) ~ Infestation +
                                       frailty(Guinea_Pig, distribution = "gaussian"),
                                     data = x,
                                     x = TRUE,
                                     y = TRUE,
                                     ties = "efron"
                                     )
    
    ## No fixed proportional hazard + frailty model
    CoxPH_tt <- fit_cox_tt(x)
    
      ### Combine the output of all models
      model_list <- list("Mod_cluster" = CoxPH_cluster,
                         "Mod_frailty" = CoxPH_frailty,
                         "Mod_frailty_timevarying" = CoxPH_tt
                         )
  
      ### Check all models for compliance with proportional hazard assumption (p >= 0.05 means true)
      CoxPHAss <- model_list %>%
        lapply(., function(xx) {
          safe_cox_zph(xx)
          })
      
      ### Compare all the Cox proportional hazard models
      CoxPHmodComp <- compare_cox_models(model_list) %>%
        as.data.frame(.) %>%
        mutate(., "Smallest_AIC" = c(.$AIC == min(.$AIC)))
      
  #-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          
  # Make a decision based on assumption check, whether to apply time interaction, or not
  aa <- DecisionMaking(Table = CoxPHAss,
                       AIC = CoxPHmodComp)
    
  #-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   
  # Here we acquire further information on our data with the chosen model    
    ## Pairwise comparison of all factor levels
    if (aa == 3) {
      pairCompCoxPH <- pairwise_tt_contrasts(model_list[[aa]])
      
      HazRat <- "AHR integrated in pairCompCoxPH"
    } else {
      pairCompCoxPH <- emmeans::lsmeans(model_list[[aa]], pairwise ~ Infestation, adjust = "BH")
      
      ## Hazard Ratio (HR) for Cox proportional hazard model without random factor
      HazRat <- cbind("HR" = summary(model_list[[aa]])$coef %>%
                        as.data.frame(.) %>%
                        dplyr::filter(grepl("Infestation", rownames(.))) %>%
                        .[, "coef"] %>%
                        exp(.),
                      
                      exp(confint(model_list[[aa]])),
                      
                      "p-value" = summary(model_list[[aa]])$coef %>%
                        as.data.frame(.) %>%
                        dplyr::filter(grepl("Infestation", rownames(.))) %>% 
                        dplyr::select(any_of(c("Pr(>|z|)", "p"))) %>%
                        set_colnames("p-value")
                      ) %>%
        as.data.frame(.) %>%
          mutate("sig." = symnum(
            .$`p-value`,
            cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
            symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "+", " "),
            abbr.colnames = FALSE,
            na = ""
          )) %>%
        mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
        mutate(., across("p-value", ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", .x))) %>%
        tibble:: rownames_to_column(., var = "Factor")
    }
      
  #-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # If proportional hazard assumption is violated and tt() is included
    if (aa == 3) {
      
      # Step wise AHR according to time points----------------------------------
      HRbyT <- map_dfr(attr(CoxPH_tt, "dummy_names"), function(dummy) {
        
        # Extract the mapping table that links dummy columns to original factor levels
        level_map   <- attr(CoxPH_tt, "level_map")
        
        # Gather all unique observed time points from your raw data vector to loop through
        time_points <- sort(c(0, unique(x$Hours_pi))) 
        
        # Pull the complete vector of beta coefficients from the model
        model_coef <- coef(CoxPH_tt)
        
        # Pull the full variance-covariance matrix from the model
        # This contains the variances on the diagonal and covariances on the off-diagonals
        model_vcov <- vcov(CoxPH_tt)
      
        # Construct the exact string name survival uses for the interaction term
        # Example: "tt(Infestation2nd)"
        tt_name <- paste0("tt(", dummy, ")")
        
        # Look up the clean, original factor level string for final reporting
        # Example: Maps "Infestation2nd" down to just "2nd"
        factor_level <- level_map %>% 
          dplyr::filter(dummy == !!dummy) %>% 
          pull(Infestation)
        
        # Extract the specific beta coefficient values from the model vector
        beta_main <- model_coef[dummy]    # Main effect beta
        beta_tt   <- model_coef[tt_name]  # Time-interaction beta
        
        # Extract specific variance and covariance values from the matrix
        # These are needed to calculate mathematically sound standard errors over time
        var_main    <- model_vcov[dummy, dummy]     # Variance of main effect
        var_tt      <- model_vcov[tt_name, tt_name] # Variance of interaction effect
        cov_main_tt <- model_vcov[dummy, tt_name]   # Covariance between main and interaction
        
        
        # 3. INNER LOOP: CALCULATE HAZARD RATIOS FOR EACH TIME POINT
        map_dfr(time_points, function(t) {
          
          # CRITICAL: Scale the time point 't' using your model's exact tt_fun logic
          # Your model used log(pmax(t, 1)), so your multiplier must match exactly
          t_scaled <- log(pmax(t, 1))
          
          # Calculate the combined log-hazard ratio at this specific scaled time point
          log_hr <- beta_main + (beta_tt * t_scaled)
          
          # Delta Method Variance Formula: Var(A + bB) = Var(A) + b^2*Var(B) + 2*b*Cov(A,B)
          # We take the square root of the final variance to get the Standard Error (SE)
          se_log_hr <- sqrt(var_main + ((t_scaled^2) * var_tt) + (2 * t_scaled * cov_main_tt))
          
          # Convert log scale metrics back to traditional Hazard Ratios (Exponentiation)
          ahr    <- exp(log_hr)                         # Adjusted Hazard Ratio point estimate
          low_ci <- exp(log_hr - (1.96 * se_log_hr))    # Lower 95% Confidence Interval limit
          upp_ci <- exp(log_hr + (1.96 * se_log_hr))    # Upper 95% Confidence Interval limit
          
          # Package values into a structured, tidy format for the current row
          tibble(
            Infestation_Level = factor_level,
            Time_Point        = paste0(t, "h_pi"),
            Hours             = t,
            Adjusted_HR       = ahr,
            Lower_95_CI       = low_ci,
            Upper_95_CI       = upp_ci,
            HR_String         = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f - %.2f)", ahr, low_ci, upp_ci)
          )
        })
      })

      # When AHR becomes 1------------------------------------------------------
      AHRis <- map_dfr(attr(CoxPH_tt, "dummy_names"), function(dummy) {
  
        # Extract the mapping table that links dummy columns to original factor levels
        level_map   <- attr(CoxPH_tt, "level_map")
        
        # Pull the complete vector of beta coefficients from the model
        model_coef <- coef(CoxPH_tt)
        
        # Construct the interaction term name
        tt_name <- paste0("tt(", dummy, ")")
        
        # Fetch clean factor label mapping
        factor_level <- level_map %>% 
          dplyr::filter(dummy == !!dummy) %>% 
          pull(Infestation)
        
        # Extract specific coefficients for this level
        beta_main <- model_coef[dummy]
        beta_tt   <- model_coef[tt_name]
        
        # Math Breakdown:
        # Setting log_hr = 0 -> beta_main + (beta_tt * log(t)) = 0
        # Solving for log(t) -> log(t) = -beta_main / beta_tt
        # Solving for original hours t -> t = exp(-beta_main / beta_tt)
        scaled_inflection_time <- -1 * beta_main / beta_tt
        actual_hours_pi        <- exp(scaled_inflection_time)
        
        # Return structured findings
        tibble(
          Infestation_Level      = factor_level,
          Main_Effect_Beta       = beta_main,
          Interaction_Beta       = beta_tt,
          Log_Scaled_Time        = scaled_inflection_time,
          Hours_At_HR_1          = actual_hours_pi
        )
      })
        
      # Step wise AHR according to time points for the plot
      AHR <- map_dfr(attr(CoxPH_tt, "dummy_names"), function(dummy) {
        
        # Extract the mapping table that links dummy columns to original factor levels
        level_map   <- attr(CoxPH_tt, "level_map")
        
        # Gather all unique observed time points from your raw data vector to loop through
        time_points <- seq(min(x$Hours_pi[x$Event == 1]),
                           max(x$Hours_pi[x$Event == 1]),
                           1) 
        
        # Pull the complete vector of beta coefficients from the model
        model_coef <- coef(CoxPH_tt)
        
        # Pull the full variance-covariance matrix from the model
        # This contains the variances on the diagonal and covariances on the off-diagonals
        model_vcov <- vcov(CoxPH_tt)
      
        # Construct the exact string name survival uses for the interaction term
        # Example: "tt(Infestation2nd)"
        tt_name <- paste0("tt(", dummy, ")")
        
        # Look up the clean, original factor level string for final reporting
        # Example: Maps "Infestation2nd" down to just "2nd"
        factor_level <- level_map %>% 
          dplyr::filter(dummy == !!dummy) %>% 
          pull(Infestation)
        
        # Extract the specific beta coefficient values from the model vector
        beta_main <- model_coef[dummy]    # Main effect beta
        beta_tt   <- model_coef[tt_name]  # Time-interaction beta
        
        # Extract specific variance and covariance values from the matrix
        # These are needed to calculate mathematically sound standard errors over time
        var_main    <- model_vcov[dummy, dummy]     # Variance of main effect
        var_tt      <- model_vcov[tt_name, tt_name] # Variance of interaction effect
        cov_main_tt <- model_vcov[dummy, tt_name]   # Covariance between main and interaction
        
          
          # 3. INNER LOOP: CALCULATE HAZARD RATIOS FOR EACH TIME POINT
          map_dfr(time_points, function(t) {
            
            # CRITICAL: Scale the time point 't' using your model's exact tt_fun logic
            # Your model used log(pmax(t, 1)), so your multiplier must match exactly
            t_scaled <- log(pmax(t, 1))
            
            # Calculate the combined log-hazard ratio at this specific scaled time point
            log_hr <- beta_main + (beta_tt * t_scaled)
            
            # Delta Method Variance Formula: Var(A + bB) = Var(A) + b^2*Var(B) + 2*b*Cov(A,B)
            # We take the square root of the final variance to get the Standard Error (SE)
            se_log_hr <- sqrt(var_main + ((t_scaled^2) * var_tt) + (2 * t_scaled * cov_main_tt))
            
            # Convert log scale metrics back to traditional Hazard Ratios (Exponentiation)
            ahr    <- exp(log_hr)                         # Adjusted Hazard Ratio point estimate
            low_ci <- exp(log_hr - (1.96 * se_log_hr))    # Lower 95% Confidence Interval limit
            upp_ci <- exp(log_hr + (1.96 * se_log_hr))    # Upper 95% Confidence Interval limit
            
            # Package values into a structured, tidy format for the current row
            tibble(
              Infestation_Level = factor_level,
              Time_Point        = paste0(t, "h_pi"),
              Hours             = t,
              Adjusted_HR       = ahr,
              Lower_95_CI       = low_ci,
              Upper_95_CI       = upp_ci,
              HR_String         = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f - %.2f)", ahr, low_ci, upp_ci)
            )
          })
        })
        
        # Uses a medium gray background to balance contrast for both bright and dark lines------------------------------
        AHRplot <-ggplot(AHR, aes(x = Hours, y = Adjusted_HR, color = Infestation_Level)) +
          geom_line(linewidth = 1.5, linetype = "solid") +
          scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "viridis") + 
          scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, ceiling(max(AHR$Hours, na.rm = TRUE) / 10) * 10)) +
          scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, ceiling(max(AHR$Adjusted_HR, na.rm = TRUE) / 10) * 10)) +
          geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
          geom_vline(data = AHRis, aes(xintercept = Hours_At_HR_1, color = Infestation_Level), 
                     linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 1, show.legend = FALSE) +
          theme_grey() + # Restores standard grey baseline
          theme(
            panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#8a8a8a"),  # True medium gray panel
            plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#e0e0e0"),   # Light gray outer canvas
            panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#b0b0b0"), # Light grid lines for visibility
            panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "#9e9e9e"),
            text = element_text(color = "black"),               # Dark text for medium gray reading
            axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
            legend.background = element_rect(fill = "#e0e0e0"),
            legend.key = element_rect(fill = "#8a8a8a")         # Keys match the plot canvas
          )
              
          } else {
            
            HRbyT <- "No time dependent PH"
            AHRis <- "No time dependent PH"
            AHRplot <- "No time dependent PH"
          }    
             
  #-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    # Outlier analysis
    # Visual inspection by graphing
    OutMart <- resid(model_list[[aa]], type = "martingale") %>% 
      as.data.frame() %>% 
      tibble::rownames_to_column(., var = "Index") %>% 
      rename("Residuals" = ".") %>%
      mutate(., across(where(is.character), as.numeric))
    
    OutMartPlot <- ggplot(OutMart, aes(x = Index, y = Residuals)) + 
      geom_point(shape=1, fill="white", color="black", size=3) +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,nrow(OutMart)), n.breaks = 7) +
      labs(x = "Observation", y = "Martingale residual") +
      theme_bw()
    
    OutDev <- resid(model_list[[aa]], type = "deviance") %>% 
      as.data.frame() %>% 
      tibble::rownames_to_column(., var = "Index") %>% 
      rename("Residuals" = ".") %>%
      mutate(., across(where(is.character), as.numeric))
    
    OutDevPlot <- ggplot(OutDev, aes(x = Index, y = Residuals)) + 
      geom_point(shape=1, fill = "white", color = "black", size = 2) +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,nrow(OutMart)), n.breaks = 7) +
      labs(x = "Observation", y = "Deviance residual") +
      theme_bw()
    
    OutlierPlot <- ggarrange(OutMartPlot, OutDevPlot,
                             labels = c("A", "B"),
                             ncol = 2, nrow = 1)
    
    # Get a list of sorted Martingale and Deviance residuals to identify the outliers
    OutLieM <- sort(resid(model_list[[aa]], type = "martingale"))
    OutLieD <- sort(resid(model_list[[aa]], type = "deviance"))
    
    # x[c(as.numeric(names(OutLieM))),] # Use this to see where the outliers came from
    
    
  # Influential observations' test
    # Check if tt() was applied to model
    DFBETAS <- names(
      as.data.frame(
        model.matrix(model_list[[aa]]))) %>%
      { if ("tt(InfNum)" %in% .) {
        
        # Get the dfbetas from the model
        resid(model_list[[aa]], type = "dfbetas") %>% 
          as.data.frame(.) %>% 
          .[order(as.numeric(rownames(.))),] %>% 
          as.data.frame(.) %>%
          .[, 1:ncol(.)-1] %>%
          as.data.frame(.)
        
      } else {
        
        # Get the dfbetas from the model
        resid(model_list[[aa]], type = "dfbetas") %>% 
          as.data.frame(.) %>% 
          .[order(as.numeric(rownames(.))),] %>% 
          as.data.frame(.)
      } }
    
    # Get the predictor factor levels minus the reference they are compared to
    InfLev <- names(
      as.data.frame(
        model.matrix(model_list[[aa]])))[grepl("Infestation", names(as.data.frame(model.matrix(model_list[[aa]]))))] %>%
        gsub("(Infestation)", "\\1: ", .)
    
    # Build influential observation plots
      # Generate plots
      DFBETAS2 <- DFBETAS %>% 
        set_colnames(InfLev) %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column(., var = "Index") %>% 
        mutate(., across(where(is.character), as.numeric))
    
      # Renders all the plots  
      InfObs <- lapply(InfLev, function(aa) {
        ggplot(DFBETAS2, aes(x = Index, y = !!sym(aa))) + 
          geom_point(shape = 1, 
                     fill  = "white", 
                     color = "black", 
                     size  = 2) +
          geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.2, -0.2),
                     color = "red",
                     linetype = "dashed",
                     linewidth = 1) +
          scale_x_continuous(limits   = c(0, nrow(DFBETAS2)), 
                             n.breaks = ceiling(nrow(DFBETAS2) / 100)) +
          theme_bw()
      })
      
      # Renders all the plots  
      InfObsPlot <- ggarrange(plotlist = InfObs[c(1:ncol(DFBETAS))],
                              labels = letters[seq( from = 1, to = ncol(DFBETAS))],
                              ncol = ifelse(ncol(DFBETAS) == 1, 1, 2), 
                              nrow = ceiling(length(InfObs)/2))
      
      # Identifies influential observations (defined as either dfbeta > 0.2 or < -0.2) within the data table (DatSurInt)
      SUB <- list("Obs_>0.2" = DFBETAS[order(as.numeric(rownames(DFBETAS))),] > 0.2,
                  "Obs_<-0.2" = DFBETAS[order(as.numeric(rownames(DFBETAS))),] < -0.2)

  #-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          
  # Collate test assumption check check and test output table
  Res.CoxPH <- list("Cox PH model chosen"                 = names(model_list[aa]),
                    "Cox PH model output"                 = model_list[[aa]],
                    "Cox model compaison (AIC)"           = CoxPHmodComp,
                    "Assumption test"                     = CoxPHAss, 
                    "Pairwise comparison"                 = pairCompCoxPH,
                    "Adjusted Hazard Ratio"               = HazRat,
                    # Information only for tt() inclusion
                    "Stepwise AHR"                        = HRbyT,
                    "Time when AHR = 1"                   = AHRis,
                    "Stepwise AHR plot"                   = AHRplot,
                    # Model behavior assessment
                    "Outliers Plot"                       = OutlierPlot,
                    "Outliers (Martingale Residuals)"     = OutLieM,
                    "Outliers (Deviance Residuals)"       = OutLieD,
                    "Influential Observations Plot"       = InfObsPlot,
                    "Influential Observations"            = SUB)
})
```

```{r comparing-different-tick-species-removal-profiles, include = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
# This is for the comparison of tick removal profiles of different tick species on guinea pigs
# This section collats data sets together for further analysis below
## Get the Rep_Exp data sets only
DatSurRep <- DatSur[grep("Rep_Exp", names(DatSur))]

## Pair data sets by name with the I_scapularis one
Pairs <- lapply(names(DatSurRep[-grep("I_scapularis", names(DatSurRep))]), function(xx) {
  
  list(names(DatSurRep[grep("I_scapularis", names(DatSurRep))]), xx) %>%
    unlist(.)
}) %>%
  purrr::set_names(names(DatSurRep[-grep("I_scapularis", names(DatSurRep))]))

## Combines the two data sets into a single dataframe
DatSurComp <- lapply(Pairs, function(qq) {
  
  bind_rows(
    list(DatSurRep[[qq[1]]],
         DatSurRep[[qq[2]]]) %>%
      purrr::set_names(qq %>%
                         sub(".*Rep_Exp_", "", .)),
    .id = "Data_Source") %>%
    mutate(., "Groups" = paste(.[["Data_Source"]], .[["Infestation"]], sep = "_")) %>%
    droplevels(.) %>%
    mutate(., across(where(is.character), as.factor)) %>%
    mutate(Groups = fct_relevel(Groups, c("I_scapularis_1st", "I_scapularis_2nd", "I_scapularis_3rd")))
})

# Tidy up what you do not need anymore
rm(DatSurRep, Pairs)
```

```{r cox-proportional-hazard-model-for-pairs, include = FALSE, cache = TRUE, cache.extra = file.mtime('Survival_Data.xlsx'), dev = 'png', fig.show = 'hide'}

# Cox proportional hazard model for comparison to I. scapularis-----------------
# This assess two things, whether guinea pigs represent a level two unit as multiple ticks are placed per guinea pig, and that guinea pigs were repeatedly used in consecutive infestations
ResCoxComp <- lapply(DatSurComp, function(xx) {
  
  ## Cluster-robust inference for repeated ticks within guinea pig
  CoxPH_cluster <- survival::coxph(Surv(Hours_pi, Event) ~ Groups,
                                   data = xx,
                                   x = TRUE,
                                   y = TRUE,
                                   ties = "efron",
                                   cluster = xx$Guinea_Pig
                                   )
  
    ### Check all models for compliance with proportional hazard assumption (p >= 0.05 means true)
    CoxPHAss <- safe_cox_zph(CoxPH_cluster)
      
  ## Here we acquire further information on our data with the chosen model    
    ## Pairwise comparison of all factor levels
    pairCompCoxPH <- emmeans::lsmeans(CoxPH_cluster, pairwise ~ Groups, adjust = "BH") %>%
      .[["contrasts"]] %>% 
      as.data.frame() %>%
      dplyr::filter(str_detect(.[, "contrast"], "(1st|2nd|3rd).*\\1")) %>%
      mutate("sig." = ifelse(.$p.value < 0.0001, "****",
                           ifelse(.$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                                  ifelse(.$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                                         ifelse(.$p.value <= 0.05, "*",
                                                ifelse(.$p.value < 0.1, "+", "")))))) %>%
      mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
      mutate(., across("p.value", ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", .x)))
      
  #-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          
  # Collate test assumption check check and test output table
  Res.CoxPH <- list("Cox PH model output"                 = CoxPH_cluster,
                    "Assumption test"                     = CoxPHAss, 
                    "Pairwise comparison"                 = pairCompCoxPH
                    )
})
```

```{r create-output-table, include = FALSE}
# Produce tables of the pairwise Cox PH models
mapply(function(aa, bb) {
  mapply(function(yy, zz) {
    # Get the pairwise comparison for each survival plot
    if (length(yy[["Pairwise comparison"]]) != 2) {
        
        Pairwise <- yy[["Pairwise comparison"]] %>%
          mutate("sig." = symnum(
            .$p.adj,
            cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
            symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "+", " "),
            abbr.colnames = FALSE,
            na = ""
          )) %>%
          mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
          mutate(., across(c("p.value", "p.adj"), ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", .x)))
        
      } else {
        
        Pairwise <- yy[["Pairwise comparison"]][["contrasts"]] %>%
          as.data.frame() %>%
          mutate("sig." = symnum(
            .$p.value,
            cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
            symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "+", " "),
            abbr.colnames = FALSE,
            na = ""
          )) %>%
          mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
          mutate(., across("p.value", ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", .x)))
      }
    
    # Turn it into a table
    gtsave(data =
           Pairwise %>%
             as.data.frame() %>%
             # Build a table
             gt() %>%
             tab_header(
               title = md("**Pairwise Comparison**"),
               subtitle = zz
               ) %>%
             tab_style(
               style = cell_text(align = "center"),
               locations = cells_column_labels()),
           filename = paste0(zz, "_PW", ".png"),
           path = paste(here(), "Output", "Tables", "Survival", bb, sep = "/"))
    
    
  }, yy = aa,
     zz = names(aa) %>%
                  sub(paste0(".*", bb), "", .))
}, aa = lapply(c("Rep_Exp", "E_collar", "FTY720"), function(zz) {
          ResCox[grepl(zz,  names(ResCox))]
        }) %>%
  purrr::set_names(c("Rep_Exp", "E_collar", "FTY720")),
   bb = c("Rep_Exp_", "E_collar_", "FTY720_"))

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Produce tables of the adjusted hazard ratios

  mapply(function(yy, zz) {
    # Get the pairwise comparison for each survival plot

        AHR <- yy[["Pairwise comparison"]] %>%
          mutate("sig." = symnum(
            .$p.adj,
            cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
            symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "+", " "),
            abbr.colnames = FALSE,
            na = ""
          )) %>%
          mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
          mutate(., across(c("p.value", "p.adj"), ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", .x)))
        
      } else {
        
        AHR <- yy[["Adjusted Hazard Ratio"]]
      }
    
    # Turn it into a table
    gtsave(data =
           AHR %>%
             as.data.frame() %>%
             # Build a table
```
